definitions.explanation: A small, narrow body of flowing water, smaller than a river. Often found in natural settings like mountains, forests, or rural areas.

examples.japanese: {森|もり}の{中|なか}を{小川|おがわ}が{流|なが}れている。
examples.english: A stream flows through the forest.

examples.japanese: {小川|おがわ}で{魚|さかな}を{捕|と}った。
examples.english: I caught fish in the stream.

examples.japanese: {小川|おがわ}のせせらぎが{聞|き}こえる。
examples.english: I can hear the murmuring of the brook.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{小川|おがわ}で{水遊|みずあそ}びをしている。
examples.english: The children are playing in the stream.

examples.japanese: {大雨|おおあめ}が{降|ふ}ると、この{小川|おがわ}は{増水|ぞうすい}して{危|あぶ}ないので{近|ちか}づかないでください。
examples.english: When it rains heavily, this stream swells and becomes dangerous, so please stay away.

notes:
FORMATION:
{小|お} (small) + {川|かわ/がわ} (river)
→ A small river; stream

USAGE:
Often appears in poetic or scenic descriptions:
・{小川|おがわ}のせせらぎ (murmur/babble of a brook)
・{小川|おがわ}の{流|なが}れ (flow of a stream)

NOTE ON NAME:
{小川|おがわ} is also a common Japanese surname (Ogawa).

RELATED WORDS BY SIZE:
・{川|かわ} - River (general term)
・{大河|たいが} - Great river, major river
・{小川|おがわ} - Stream, brook
・{細流|さいりゅう/ほそながれ} - Rivulet, streamlet (literary)

ONOMATOPOEIA:
・さらさら - Flowing smoothly (stream sound)
・せせらぎ - Murmuring, babbling (of a brook)
